title: Scam patterns affecting seniors and Singapore's anti-scam measures
asked: Dr Choo Pei Ling asked whether any recent patterns have been observed in scams targeting seniors and, if so, what those patterns are.
response: In 2025, seniors aged 65 and above made up about 15% of all scam victims and were the only age group whose victim numbers rose from 2024, losing about $37,000 each on average, the highest of any age group. About two in five senior victims fell for investment or government official impersonation scams. The Police do not track recovered scam proceeds by age group, and recovery is difficult once money leaves Singapore; measures include international law enforcement collaboration and cryptocurrency tracing. The reply also set out five thrusts: OCHA powers to move upstream with online platforms, work with telcos, banks and crypto service providers, a tougher penalty framework including for scam mules, public education for seniors, and international collaboration.

key_points.point: Seniors aged 65 and above were about 15% of all scam victims in 2025 and the only age group with more victims than in 2024.
key_points.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
key_points.quote: seniors aged 65 and above made up about 15% of all scam victims

key_points.point: Average loss per senior victim was about $37,000, the highest across age groups.
key_points.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
key_points.quote: Each senior lost about $37,000 on average, the highest among all age groups.

key_points.point: About two in five senior victims were taken in by investment or government official impersonation scams.
key_points.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
key_points.quote: About two in five scam victims who are seniors fell prey to investment or government official impersonation scams.

key_points.point: The Police do not break down recovered scam proceeds by age group.
key_points.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
key_points.quote: The Police do not track the amount of scam proceeds recovered by age group.

key_points.point: Recovery odds are very low once the money has left Singapore.
key_points.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
key_points.quote: Once the monies exit Singapore, the odds of it being recovered is very low.

key_points.point: Asset recovery measures include cross-border law enforcement cooperation and cryptocurrency tracing.
key_points.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
key_points.quote: strengthening international collaboration among law enforcement agencies and enhancing cryptocurrency tracing capabilities

key_points.point: Global scam losses last year exceeded US$440 billion.
key_points.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
key_points.quote: more than US$440 billion were lost to scams globally

key_points.point: Online Criminal Harms Act powers are used to work with online service providers and reduce the threat surface.
key_points.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
key_points.quote: using the powers enabled by the Online Criminal Harms Act (OCHA), we have moved upstream

key_points.point: The ministry works with telcos, banks and recognised and authorised crypto service providers to prevent and interdict scams.
key_points.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
key_points.quote: we work very closely with our telcos, our banks and also the recognised and authorised crypto service providers

key_points.point: The penalty framework was enhanced to deter perpetrators operating in Singapore, and a framework targets scam mules.
key_points.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
key_points.quote: we have also enhanced our penalty framework to deter perpetrators from operating in Singapore

key_points.point: Public education, including for seniors, shares the latest modus operandi and preventive practices.
key_points.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
key_points.quote: public education – extensive public education, including for our seniors

key_points.point: International collaboration with governments, jurisdictions and law enforcement agencies is being stepped up, including intelligence sharing.
key_points.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
key_points.quote: we are stepping up international collaboration with governments, with jurisdictions, with law enforcement agencies

key_points.point: The Police do track total scam proceeds recovered, just not by age group.
key_points.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
key_points.quote: Yes, indeed, the Police do track the amount of scam proceeds recovered. We just do not track them by age group.

key_points.point: Recovered proceeds are a small share of total losses.
key_points.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
key_points.quote: the amount of scam proceeds that have been recovered are a small proportion compared to the overall amount of monies that is lost

key_points.point: Prevention is described as better than pursuing recovery afterwards.
key_points.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
key_points.quote: prevention is better than the follow-up pursuit of recovering monies

left_open: Specific targets or timelines for shortening the time between scam detection and intervention, such as freezing funds or disrupting scam flows
Specific safeguards against social engineering tactics that exploit trust, urgency and fear among seniors
The exact total amount of scam proceeds recovered
supplementary: Supplementary questions covered system design against evolving scam typologies, coordination between banks, telcos and enforcement agencies, and safeguards against social engineering.
